description.narrative:
The overall objective of the project is contribution to the enhanced competitiveness and sustainable socio-economic development in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The project is designed to contribute to more developed and equal opportunity society in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It aims to promote and support improvements through identifying innovative potential in the country and engaging it for social advancements leading towards economic development.
The specific objective is to improve risk sharing funding for innovative and/or inclusive businesses.
The project will contribute to reduction of unemployment and poverty utilizing innovative and sustainable approach.

Projektet syftar till att främja och stödja förbättringen av landets ekonomi genom att identifiera innovativ potential i landet och engagera den för sociala framsteg och ekonomisk utveckling. Utmaningsfonden underlättar riktade åtgärder för att ge stöd till innovation och frigöra ekonomisk potential bland kapaciterade aktörer. Den är baserad på mycket konkurrenskraftiga och transparenta förfaranden för att säkerställa ett neutralt tillvägagångssätt och stimulera tillväxt

The project aims to promote and support the improvement of country´s economy through Identifying innovative potential and engaging it for social advancement and economic development. The Challenge Fund facilitates targeted action to prompt support to innovation and unlock economic potential among capacitated players. It is based on highly competitive and transparent procedures to ensure non-bias approach and stimulate growth.

The Challenge to Change 3.0 (C2C3) intervention achieved substantial results in strengthening innovation capacity, competitiveness, and sustainable growth among SMEs in Bosnia and Herzegovina through a market-based, co-financed Challenge Fund mechanism. The project generated exceptionally strong demand from the private sector, receiving 1,110 applications across four Calls for Proposals. Following a rigorous two-stage evaluation process, 66 grant agreements were signed and 59 projects were successfully completed. Total investments amounted to EUR 4.11 million, combining EUR 1.36 million in grants with EUR 2.75 million in beneficiary co-financing, demonstrating a strong leverage effect where development assistance successfully mobilised private capital rather than replacing it. At the enterprise level, the intervention produced measurable economic and operational improvements. Supported SMEs reported increased productivity, improved efficiency, diversification of products and services, and expansion into approximately 60 new markets. Employment outcomes were also significant, with the project contributing to the retention of 1,242 jobs and the creation of 185 new jobs, including opportunities specifically benefiting women and young people. Investments in digital transformation and green economy solutions further strengthened operational resilience and sustainability. The project successfully established and operationalised a robust risk-sharing financing mechanism through the Challenge Fund. The intervention addressed a critical financing gap affecting innovative SMEs, particularly those lacking access to traditional investment capital due to perceived risk and limited market confidence. By requiring mandatory beneficiary co-financing of at least 50%, the project effectively ensured that supported investments reflected genuine market demand and business commitment. Supported enterprises introduced new products, services, production processes, and environmentally sustainable solutions across multiple sectors, including manufacturing, Information and Communication Technologies (ICT), agriculture, recycling, and design industries. The evaluation framework successfully integrated innovation, feasibility, social impact, green economy, digital transformation, gender equality, and alignment with Sustainable Development Goals, thereby ensuring that selected projects contributed to broader development priorities. The interventions results also aligned closely with its socio-economic development goals. Employment creation and retention targets were achieved despite challenging economic conditions characterised by inflationary pressures, labour shortages, and broader macroeconomic instability. The support mechanism strengthened SME resilience and competitiveness by enabling enterprises to modernise operations, improve energy efficiency, diversify exports, and enter new markets. Importantly, the project succeeded not only at the enterprise level but also at the systemic level. The establishment of transparent governance procedures, independent evaluation structures, digital application and monitoring systems, and rigorous anti-corruption safeguards significantly strengthened institutional capacities of the implementing partners. The upgraded digital (eMSAE) platform, comprehensive grant manual, procurement procedures, and monitoring frameworks created operational tools and institutional knowledge that can support future interventions.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
